commits.message:
A joiner always draws its seam, lifting the fg off a bg it would vanish into (rich-joiners-er38.0jr) (#515)

* Pin 0.24.1's bytes for joins whose every seam cell already shows (rich-joiners-er38.0jr)

* A joiner always draws its seam, lifting the fg off a bg it would vanish into (rich-joiners-er38.0jr)

* A lifted seam ink is the entry the depth draws, and the docs say where the floor is blind (rich-joiners-er38.0jr)

The lift measured each step as the depth draws it but returned the
unrounded step, so below truecolor a cell carried a colour one 8-bit unit
off its ground that only cleared the floor after rounding. An export reads
a recording in truecolor and drew that seam invisible. The lift now returns
the colour it measured; the bytes at the render's own depth are unchanged.

docs/strip.md promised a seam shows "whatever the neighbours' colours". A
theme slot beside a fixed colour has no RGB the render can measure, so it is
drawn as it is; the page now says so.

* docs(strip): the seam floor holds as far as a render can see both colours (rich-joiners-er38.0jr)

A cap on the terminal's own background, or a notch in reverse video over it,
has a side no render knows, and is drawn as it is. The page opened by
promising every joiner cell stands off its ground.

* A vanishing seam ink steps in the kind the depth draws it, so a cube entry is never parted from its ground by a slot (rich-joiners-er38.0jr)

The lift chose slot or RGB candidates from the ink as authored. A mix of a
slot and an RGB is the theme's colour at truecolor but a cube entry at 256,
so at 256 prism between `blue` and `#000080` measured its vanishing thirds
as cube entries and then lifted them into slots, which the floor passes
against any cube entry on the index alone: color(4) on color(18), the same
navy. Ink that vanishes is always drawn in the same kind as its ground, so
the steps are now drawn in that kind and measured the way the ink was.
